title: [RFC] 145 - Unify auth to better-auth
body:
# Unify to BetterAuth

## Background

- Clerk server-side API has high latency, causing slow data loading experience for users
- Limited customization flexibility. For example, when implementing referral features, we need to support users entering invitation codes during registration, but Clerk's built-in registration component cannot meet this requirement
- next-auth (auth.js) has been acquired by better-auth

## Goal

Unify to use better-auth as the authentication system across LobeChat open-source and cloud deployments.

## Current Status

- next-auth currently only supports SSO login, does not support email/password login

---

## Phase 1: BetterAuth Support in Open-Source (lobechat)

Add better-auth as an authentication option, with backward compatibility for next-auth environment variables.

### 1.1 BetterAuth Infrastructure

- [x] Implement sign in/sign up components
  - [x] Configure email verification in better-auth
  - [x] Implement sign-up page with email/username/password
  - [x] Implement email verification notice page
  - [x] Add i18n translations (zh-CN, en-US)
  - [x] Add SMTP configuration to .env.example
  - [x] Delete Clerk sign-up/login pages
- [ ] Support email, GitHub, Google, Apple login (email ✅, OAuth pending)

### 1.2 NextAuth Compatibility

- [ ] Ensure better-auth can reuse next-auth environment variables (e.g., `AUTH_SECRET`, OAuth client configs)
- [ ] Adapt OIDC provider to work with better-auth
- [ ] Adapt auth logic in tRPC and route handlers
- [ ] Update documentation for better-auth deployment

---

## Phase 2: Clerk Migration in Cloud (lobechat-cloud)

Migrate Clerk to better-auth in the cloud repository, then open-source the migration tools.

### 2.1 Cloud Migration

- [ ] Migrate Clerk user data to BetterAuth
- [ ] Validate migration in production environment

### 2.2 Cleanup Clerk Dependencies

- [ ] Remove Clerk code from cloud repository
- [ ] Clean up Clerk-related dependencies and environment variables

### 2.3 Open-Source Migration Tools

- [ ] Open-source Clerk → BetterAuth migration script
- [ ] Publish Clerk migration documentation

---

## Phase 3: NextAuth Migration Script in Open-Source (lobechat)

Provide migration path for existing next-auth users.

### 3.1 Migration Script

- [ ] Implement NextAuth → BetterAuth migration script
- [ ] Handle user data, sessions, and OAuth accounts migration

### 3.2 Documentation & Cleanup

- [ ] Publish NextAuth migration documentation
- [ ] Remove NextAuth code after migration period
- [ ] Clean up dependencies and environment variables

title: [RFC] 146 - New activities for user memories
body:
## Background

Activities capture time-bound, real-world events with people, places, and outcomes. Contexts describe ambient situations, identities describe people, experiences capture learnings, and preferences capture choices—none of those fully encode the “what actually happened, when, and with whom” that gives a living timeline.

- Activity vs Context: contexts are ambient (environment/state); activities are discrete events with start/end, participants, and status.
- Activity vs Identity: identities are who people are; activities show what those people did together in time and space.
- Activity vs Experience: experiences extract lessons; activities are factual sequences and stories that experiences can be distilled from.
- Activity vs Preference: preferences are enduring choices; activities are episodic events that may generate or contradict preferences.

## Activities happen in real life

Real memories are anchored to events: meetings, trips, calls, workouts, parties. Without capturing when, where, and with whom something happened (and how it felt), we miss the texture needed to ground reasoning, recommendations, and recall.

### Scenario 1: Client meeting

Fields: `title`, `activityType=meeting`, `startsAt`/`endsAt`/`timezone`, `status`, `associated_identity_ids` (attendees), `location` { `name`/`address` }, `notes` (agenda, objectives), `narrative` (what happened), `feedback` (how it felt), `tags`/`metadata`.

### Scenario 2: Doctor appointment

Fields: `activityType=appointment`, `startsAt`/`endsAt`, `status` (completed/canceled), `location`, `associated_identity_ids` (doctor), `notes` (symptoms, prep), `narrative` (visit summary), `feedback` (comfort, satisfaction), `tags`/`metadata`.

### Scenario 3: Workout session

Fields: `activityType=exercise`, `startsAt`/`endsAt`, `status`, `location` (gym/park), `notes` (plan), `narrative` (what was done), `feedback` (effort, mood), `tags`/`metadata`.

### Scenario 4: Dinner with friends

Fields: `activityType=meal/social`, `startsAt`/`endsAt`, `location`, `associated_identity_ids`, `notes` (occasion), `narrative` (conversation highlights), `feedback` (vibe), `tags`/`metadata`.

## How this is beneficial to existing memory design?

Activities provide a temporal spine that other layers can hook into. They ground identities in shared events, supply raw material for experiences (learnings), and reveal preferences from repeated patterns or feedback. They also improve retrieval: asking “what happened with Alice last week?” or “last time we discussed X” needs event-level data.

### Possible improvements

- Add lightweight joins (instead of arrays) for participant roles/weights if querying becomes heavier.
- Add derived summaries that generate experiences/preferences from narratives/feedback.
- Add optional structured location facets (city/country) for filtering without coordinates.

### Potential application

#### Recall helper

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A(Log activities with people) --> B(Score recency + feedback tone per identity)
  B --> C(Detect positive but stale relationships)
  C --> D(Suggest reach-outs with last narrative snippet)
```
> Finds who to reconnect with, using how past interactions felt, not just counts.

#### Preference drift detector

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A(Log activities with feedback) --> B(Extract implicit likes/dislikes from narrative + feedback)
  B --> C(Compare against stored preferences)
  C --> D(Flag drifts and suggest updates)
```
> Spots when lived activities contradict saved preferences, keeping the profile current.

#### Preference map

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A(Aggregate activities by type + feedback tone) --> B(Map to preference facets)
  B --> C(Visualize what contexts/people/places correlate with positive sentiment)
  C --> D(Suggest future choices aligned with observed preferences)
```
> Builds a live map of what the user tends to enjoy or avoid, grounded in actual activities.

#### Playbook of your life

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A(New task or question) --> B(Search narrative vectors for similar past activities)
  B --> C(Extract steps and outcomes)
  C --> D(Offer a ready playbook)
```
> Turns past narratives into reusable playbooks for similar future work.

#### Wellness and mood correlation

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A4(Log activities with feedback sentiment) --> B4(Correlate activity types with mood)
  B4 --> C4(Suggest better habits: more morning runs, fewer late calls)
```
> Feedback as a first-class field allows pattern mining on subjective outcomes, not just attendance.

#### Thematic memory calendar

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A5(Render activities on calendar) --> B5(Color by activityType)
  B5 --> C5(Click for narrative/feedback snippets)
  C5 --> D5(Semantic search: when did I last feel exhausted after a call?)
```
> Calendar plus semantic search gives both chronological and fuzzy recall; activities are the missing event nodes.

## Table structure (`user_memories_activities`)

> [!NOTE]
> Column names match “what happened, when, with whom, where, and how it felt,” plus semantic recall.

- `activityType`: bounded enum for quick faceting (meeting, appointment, social, trip, etc.).
- `status`: minimal lifecycle (planned, completed, canceled).
- `timezone`, `startsAt`, `endsAt`: temporal anchors; names read cleanly in code and APIs.
- `associatedIdentityIds`: array of linked identities; fastest path to attach people without a join table.
- `location` JSON: `{ name, address?, type?, tags? }` keeps place context without enforcing geocoding.
- `notes`: annotations/prep/context.
- `narrative` + `narrativeVector`: the story of the event, vectorized for semantic recall.
- `feedback` + `feedbackVector`: subjective/psychological take, vectorized for feeling-based search.
- `tags`, `metadata`: lightweight categorization and extensibility.
- `userMemoryId`, timestamps: align with other layers for ownership and access metrics.

> quote
> Names prioritize clarity over cleverness: `narrative` signals long-form story; `notes` signals short annotations; `feedback` signals subjective sentiment.

## Concerns

- Overlap with reminders/task apps: avoid turning activities into future todos; keep “planned” minimal and promote to activity only when confirmed.
- Privacy/sensitivity: feedback is subjective; ensure access controls and selective recall.
- Data quality: free-form narrative may need summarization/normalization to stay useful.
- Vector costs: narrative/feedback embeddings add storage; may need pruning/TTL or selective indexing.

title: 建议将 LobeHub Cloud 的 Google 模型 API 更换为 Vertex AI API
body:
我是 LobeHub 的用户，偶尔会使用 LobeHub Cloud，对产品有一定的了解。
在使用 Google 系列模型时，我注意到当前 Gemini API 在图像生成方面的内容限制相对较严，尤其在处理某些成人向或敏感场景时，容易触发过滤，影响使用体验。
相比之下，通过 Vertex AI（Google Cloud Vertex AI）调用这些模型时，图像生成的内容限制更宽松，能更好地支持这类需求。
因此建议 LobeHub Cloud 考虑切换或增加 Vertex AI 作为选项。
当然，我没有深入了解过 Vertex AI，如果有其他技术或兼容性问题导致无法使用的话，那就无视此条反馈好了。
author: YspritanHyzygy

title: 小小吐槽
body:
### 問題描述 / Description

我嘗試使用 LobeChat，但在兩個核心工作流上的體驗極差。相比於 Chatbox 這樣上手即用的客戶端，目前的產品邏輯顯得非常死板，配置異常繁瑣，嚴重影響使用心情。

### 具體痛點 / Pain Points

#### 1. 缺乏自動 OCR 路由 (Lack of Automatic OCR Routing)
*   **當前行為：** 當我上傳文件給不支持視覺的模型時，系統直接報錯提示「該模型不支持 OCR」。
*   **期望行為：** 系統應該具備自動路由功能。如果當前選用的模型不具備視覺能力，系統應該在後台自動調用具備視覺能力的模型（如 GPT-4o 等）先解析出文字，然後將解析後的文本內容交給當前模型處理。
*   **痛點：** 用戶根本不應該為了傳個文件還要在不同模型之間手動切來切去，這是最基礎的易用性缺失。

#### 2. 嵌入模型配置入口極其隱蔽 (Embedding Model Configuration is Impossible to Find)
*   **當前行為：** 我花費了大量時間嘗試配置知識庫。我的 API 供應商明明提供了嵌入模型 (Embedding Model)，且 Key 是有效的，但系統一直提示「未配置嵌入模型」。
*   **問題：** 我翻遍了所有的設置菜單，每一個選項都找過了，根本找不到配置嵌入模型的位置在哪裡。UI 設計完全沒有引導性，難以找到配置入口。
*   **期望行為：** 不要把這麼關鍵的配置藏得那麼深。應該在對應服務商的設置頁中提供清晰、顯眼的「嵌入模型」選擇項，或者能夠自動檢測可用模型。如果還需要用戶專門去註冊一個文字處理模型的供應商，那完全是不合理的設計。

### 總結 / Conclusion

目前產品的上手門檻高得離譜。Chatbox 雖然是很老的軟件，但人家在這些方面做得非常到位，上手非常容易。請重新審視這些基礎設置的交互體驗，現在的設計非常令人失望。

title: Help needed: Implementing a self-hosted Market server for private LobeChat deployment
body:
Hey everyone 👋

  I'm setting up a private LobeChat instance and want to run my own marketplace for agents, plugins, and MCPs rather than relying on the centralized `market.lobehub.com`.

  ### What I've discovered so far

  From digging through the codebase, I found that:

  - The `NEXT_PUBLIC_MARKET_BASE_URL` environment variable already exists and can point to a custom market server
  - The market integration uses `@lobehub/market-sdk` and `@lobehub/market-types` packages
  - The Discover service (`src/server/services/discover/index.ts`) properly passes this custom URL to the SDK

  So the infrastructure seems ready — I just need to understand how to implement a compatible server.

  ### My questions

  1. **Minimal viable market**: What's the minimum set of endpoints needed if I just want a read-only marketplace for browsing and installing agents/plugins? Do I need all of:
     - `getAssistantList`, `getAssistantDetail`, `getAssistantCategories`
     - `getPluginList`, `getPluginDetail`, `getPluginCategories`
     - `getMcpList`, `getMcpDetail`, `getMcpCategories`, `getMcpManifest`
     - `getModelList`, `getProviderList`, etc.

  2. **Authentication**: The code references M2M tokens and OIDC flows. Can I skip authentication entirely for a simple private deployment, or is it required for the SDK to function?

  3. **Static JSON alternative**: The legacy system used static JSON indexes (like `lobe-chat-agents` repo). Is there a way to use static files with the new market system, or does it require a full API server?

  4. **API schema/types**: Is there an OpenAPI spec or should I just reverse-engineer from `@lobehub/market-types`? Any gotchas I should know about?

  ### My use case

  Private family deployment where I want to curate a small set of trusted agents and plugins without exposing the instance to the public marketplace.

  ### Related

  I've also opened a documentation request: [#10762](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/issues/10762)

  Has anyone else tackled self-hosting their own market? Would love to hear about your experience or any pointers from the team!

  Thanks in advance 🙏

title: 📜 [RFC] 147 - Migrate Next App Router to Vite React Router SPA
body:
## Background / 背景 当前 `src/app` 的 Next.js 应用随着功能增长，依赖与构建链路逐渐变得沉重：在"单个页面"的开发场景下，`next dev` 的编译时间通常需要 **20s+**；首个页面（例如 `/agent`）编译完成后，`next-server` 进程内存占用可达到 **8G+**；随后再编译一些必要的 tRPC/API 相关模块，内存峰值可进一步上升到 **12G+**。 这对小内存机型非常不友好；即使在 16G 内存的开发机上，也常常难以满足流畅开发的资源要求（频繁触发内存压力、系统换页、响应变慢等），直接影响日常迭代效率。 在上一次重构中，项目已基本完成从 Next Router 到 React Router 的迁移，形成了以 **React Router + SPA** 为核心的路由架构。这使得从根本上去除 Next App Router（保留必要的后端能力并用 catch-all 托管 SPA 构建产物）的方案成为可能。 ## Proposed Architecture / 目标架构 本 RFC 的核心思路是把 "web app" 拆成 **前后端两条独立的构建与运行链路**： ### Backend: Next.js Serverless Functions (保留) - 保留现有基于 Next App Router 的后端 `route.ts`（例如 `src/app/(backend)/**/route.ts`），继续以 serverless functions 形式提供： - `/api/*`、`/trpc/*`、`/webapi/*`、`/oidc/*` 等后端能力 - 现有 Auth/OIDC/tRPC 等中间层逻辑保持不变（不在本 RFC 里重构） - 仍由 Next 驱动部署（Vercel / Docker standalone / 其他 serverless 平台均可沿用既有方案） ### Frontend: Vite + React Router SPA (迁移) - 前端不再由 Next 构建，不再依赖 Next App Router 的 `page.tsx/layout.tsx/metadata.ts` 等体系。 - Vite 负责： - 依赖预构建（esbuild）与 HMR - **多入口构建**：分别输出 Desktop 和 Mobile 两个 HTML 模板 + 共享 `assets/*` - React Router 负责： - 全量路由、懒加载、错误边界、页面级布局等 - 路由组织采用约定式路由生成方案： - 使用 `vite-plugin-route-builder` 生成 React Router 路由配置：https://github.com/Innei/vite-plugin-route-builder ### ~~Variants (`[variants]`)~~ → 移除，改为 Catch-All Route 运行时注入 **决策：完全移除 `[variants]` 机制**，与 Electron Desktop 静态导出保持逻辑一致（参考 `@scripts/electronWorkflow/modifiers` 中的处理方式）。 原 `[variants]` 承载的三个职责——locale、isMobile、theme——按如下方式替代： - **theme**：已移除，不再需要服务端判定 - **locale**：由 Next.js catch-all route 在运行时通过字符串替换注入到 HTML 模板 - **isMobile**：由 Vite 多入口构建分别输出 Desktop/Mobile 两套 HTML 模板，catch-all route 根据 UA 选择返回哪个 #### HTML 模板 + Magic Comment 方案 Vite 构建产出的 HTML 模板中预留 magic comment 占位符，Next.js catch-all route 在每次请求时做字符串替换： ```html
``` Next.js catch-all route handler： ```ts // src/app/(backend)/[...path]/route.ts export async function GET(req: NextRequest) { const isMobile = detectMobile(req.headers.get('user-agent')); const locale = getLocaleFromCookie(req) || 'en-US'; const dir = isRTL(locale) ? 'rtl' : 'ltr'; // 启动时读入内存缓存的 HTML 模板 const template = isMobile ? mobileHtml : desktopHtml; // 运行时注入：serverConfig 包含 feature flags、enabled providers、 // analytics config、s3FilePath、marketBaseUrl 等所有客户端需要的配置 const serverConfig = await getServerGlobalConfig(); const meta = generateSEOMeta(req.nextUrl.pathname, locale); const html = template .replace('', locale) .replace('', dir) .replace('', meta) .replace('` 注入，或客户端动态插入 `

title: mcp超时问题
body:
lobechat有没有类似trae对mcp超时的控制，例如
超时配置
stdio 类型的 MCP Server 支持通过 env 字段来设置超时时间：
```
"env": {
    "START_MCP_TIMEOUT_MS": "60000" // 启动 MCP Server 的超时时间（单位：ms）
    "RUN_MCP_TIMEOUT_MS": "60000"   // 调用 MCP Server tools 的超时时间（单位：ms）
}
```

HTTP 类型的 MCP Server 配置支持通过 headers 字段来设置超时时间：
```
"headers": {
    "START_MCP_TIMEOUT_MS": "60000" // 启动 MCP Server 的超时时间（单位：ms）
    "RUN_MCP_TIMEOUT_MS": "60000"   // 调用 MCP Server tools 的超时时间（单位：ms）
}
```

title: File embedding model configuration is global, forcing all tenants to share the same API Key
body:
### 📋 Problem Description

The current `DEFAULT_FILES_CONFIG` embedding model configuration is **globally applied**, which creates a design conflict in multi-tenant scenarios:

**Core Issue**:
- Embedding model configuration is global (`DEFAULT_FILES_CONFIG=embedding_model=zhipu/embedding-3`)
- API Key must also be configured globally (`ZHIPU_API_KEY=xxx`)
- Result: **All users are forced to share the same API Key**, preventing proper multi-tenant isolation

### 🔍 Specific Behavior

1. Admin configures environment variables:
   DEFAULT_FILES_CONFIG=embedding_model=zhipu/embedding-3
   ZHIPU_API_KEY=sk-xxx
   2. All tenants' file embeddings use this global API Key

3. Even if users configure their own zhipu API Key in the frontend, file embedding does not use it

### ⚖️ Comparison: Chat Feature

The chat feature supports users configuring their own API Keys in the frontend, achieving multi-tenant isolation. However, file embedding does not support this and only uses global configuration.

### 🚨 Issues This Causes

- ❌ Cannot achieve user-level API Key isolation
- ❌ Cannot bill per user
- ❌ Heavy usage by one user consumes the global quota
- ❌ Admin must pay for all users' embedding operations

### 📝 Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure environment variables:
   DEFAULT_FILES_CONFIG=embedding_model=zhipu/embedding-3
   2. Do NOT configure `ZHIPU_API_KEY`
3. User configures their own zhipu API Key in the frontend
4. Upload a file to knowledge base for embedding
5. **Expected**: Uses user's configured API Key
6. **Actual**: Throws `InvalidProviderAPIKey` error

title: Finer-grained data clearing: clear topics/chats without deleting assistants
body:
### Summary
When using LobeChat’s “Clear data” function, it currently clears **assistants** together with **topics/chats**. I’d like a more fine-grained data clearing option so I can **only clear topics (conversation history)** while keeping my configured assistants intact.

### Problem / Motivation
Right now, “Clear data” feels like an all-or-nothing reset:
- I often want to wipe **chat topics/history** for privacy or housekeeping.
- But I still want to keep my **assistants** (system prompts, settings, tools, icons, etc.) because re-creating them is time-consuming (and easy to lose careful configs).

This makes it hard to do routine cleanup without losing setup work.

### Current Behavior
- Using **Clear data** removes:
  - Topics / chats (expected)
  - Assistants (unexpected / undesirable for my use case)

### Expected Behavior
Provide granular options, e.g.:
- Clear **topics only** (chat history)
- Clear **assistants only**
- Clear **prompts / presets** (if applicable)
- Clear **files / knowledge base / embeddings** (if applicable)
- Clear **settings** (optional)
- Clear **cache only** (optional)
- “Clear everything” remains available as a full reset

### Proposed UX / Implementation Ideas
Possible approaches (pick one):
1. **Checkbox modal** for “Clear data”
   - `[ ] Topics / chat history`
   - `[ ] Assistants`
   - `[ ] Files/Knowledge`
   - `[ ] Settings`
   - with “Select all” + “Confirm” (type-to-confirm like `CLEAR`)
2. **Separate menu items**
   - “Clear chat history”
   - “Clear assistants”
   - “Factory reset”
3. **Export / backup prompt**
   - If the user chooses to delete assistants, show a warning + offer export first.

### Why This Matters (Use Cases)
- Privacy: wipe chats before sharing device/browser
- Housekeeping: remove cluttered topics without losing carefully tuned assistants
- QA/testing: clear conversation state while keeping assistant configs to reproduce issues faster

### Questions / Clarifications
1. Is the current “Clear data” intended to be a full reset (factory reset), or is deleting assistants an accidental side-effect?
2. Which storage mode(s) does this apply to: local storage, indexedDB, sync/cloud, multi-device?
3. Should “Clear topics only” also remove message attachments, or keep files?

### Environment (please fill if needed)
- LobeChat version: <!-- e.g. vX.Y.Z -->
- Deployment: <!-- Web / Desktop / Self-hosted -->
- Browser/OS: <!-- e.g. Chrome 120 / macOS 14 -->
- Storage: <!-- local only / sync enabled -->

title: Image generation failed in v2.x – error: JWKS_KEY environment variable is not set
body: ### 📱 Client Type Web (Desktop Browser) ### 💻 Operating System Windows ### 📦 Deployment Platform Self hosting Docker ### 🔧 Deployment Mode server db (lobe-chat-database image) ### 📌 Version V2.0.0-next.228 ### 🌐 Browser Edge ### 🐛 Bug Description After upgrading from LobeChat v1.x to the latest v2.x (self-compiled), image generation through “Qwen Image / fal-ai-qwen-image” consistently fails with the error: > *start async task error: JWKS_KEY environment variable is not set* My local environment, network topology, and authentication method (Clerk) are **identical to the previous v1.x setup**, where image generation worked normally. No configuration changes were made other than rebuilding the newest version. This suggests a regression or a new mandatory dependency on `JWKS_KEY` in v2.x that was not required before. ### 📷 Recurrence Steps 1. Run LobeChat **v2.x** in the same deployment as v1.x * Authentication: **Clerk** * Deployment: internal network (intranet domain pointing to LAN) 2. Open any workflow that calls **fal-ai/qwen-image** with prompt such as: * “a cute cat” 3. Click generate image 4. The task fails immediately with: ``` Generation Failed start async task error: **JWKS_KEY environment variable is not set** ``` ### 🚦 Expected Behavior * The system should generate images the same way as in **v1.x** without requiring additional environment variables that were previously optional. ### 📝 Additional Information * My LobeChat instance is running in a **closed internal network**. * Although a custom domain is configured, that domain also resolves **only inside the LAN**. * The project uses **Clerk for identity verification**. * I rebuilt/compiled the latest **v2.x** with: * Network and `.env` configuration **unchanged** * Same GPU / Docker / plugin settings as before Suggested root cause hypothesis: * v2.x may have introduced a hard requirement on `JWKS_KEY` when starting async image tasks. * Documentation does not clearly mention this as required for intranet deployments using Clerk. ### 🛠️ Willing to Submit a PR? title: Problem with SearXNG and Ollama
body:
Hi all,

I am using the Community Edition of LobeHub, version 1.143.2, and have set up the system as described at https://lobehub.com/de/docs/self-hosting/platform/docker-compose.

SearXNG is enabled in the environment file (SEARCH_PROVIDERS=searxng) and is available at http://searxng:8080 (as configured in the Compose file). When I log in to the lobe-chat container, the command ‘wget -O - http://searxng:8080/search?q=test&format=json’ also returns a usable response as expected. Therefore, everything should be able to function.

Only the language models provided by my Ollama server are available as LLMs, including ‘command-r’.

In my settings, under ‘Default Assistant -> Model Settings’ and everywhere under ‘Default Assistant’, I have entered ‘command-r’ as the language model.

However, since queries such as ‘How did the Oilers play against the Maple Leafs on 4 February 2026? Use Web search!’ were always answered with something like "...unable to complete your request... no real-time access to information from the future..." – meaning that SearXNG was not being used – I installed https://github.com/hezhijie0327/chat-plugin-searxng-search as a plugin and configured http://searxng:8080 as the backend there as well.

But the fact remains that I get the same (or at least a very similar) answer.

Even changing the language model (command-r:latest, deepseek-ocr:3b, deepseek-r1:14b, embeddinggemma:latest, gemma3:4b, gemma3n:e4b, glm-4.7-flash:q4_K_M, lfm2.5-thinking:laest, ministral-3:14b, nemotron-3-nano:30b, olfh/teuken-7b-instruct-commercial-v0.4:latest, qooba/qwen3-coder-30b-a3b-instruct:q3_k_m, qwen3-coder:30b and qwen3:4b) does not change the situation.

I have no idea how LobeChat, Ollama, LLM and SearXNG should interact here, but nothing in the request that LobeChat sends to Ollama or in the response indicates that a web search should be performed via SearXNG or what the query should look like exactly.

I attached a file showing how request and response looked.

What did I miss?

Thanks for your support,
Michael

不过考虑到 RustFS 目前仍处于相对早期的阶段，在我朋友和我进行 RustFS 试用部署期间需要边部署边排错，且实例空载时也会产生大量日志（每小时一个文件，每个文件约 2.3MB ）。基于现状来看 RustFS 在生产环境的稳定性、社区活跃度和文档完善程度暂时还难以达到预期，因此在完成试用评估后，暂无计划将其用于生产部署。同时考虑到数据安全性以及充分利用现有计算资源的因素，也暂时不考虑继续使用 MinIO 以及各类云对象存储服务。

title: [RFC] 150 - Progressive Tool Loading (Tools 渐进式加载)
body:
## 背景 / 动机

### 当前问题

当 Agent 启用了大量工具（MCP servers、builtin tools、plugins）时，**所有**工具的完整 schema 和 system role 会在对话开始前一次性全量注入上下文：

```
当前行为（全量加载）：
├── tools[] 参数：所有工具的 JSON Schema（function calling）
└── system message：所有工具的 systemRole 文本
```

这带来了几个问题：

1. **上下文膨胀** — 每个工具的 JSON Schema + system role 约 2-5KB，20-30 个工具就是 50-100KB+ 的上下文，用户还没发消息就已经占满了
2. **Token 浪费** — 大多数对话只用到 2-3 个工具，却要为所有已启用工具付出 token 开销
3. **质量下降** — 过多的系统上下文会分散模型注意力，降低响应质量
4. **成本问题** — 用户为从未使用的工具 schema 支付 input token 费用

社区的相关反馈：
- [#11915](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/issues/11915) — 多个 Bug 报告中提到 token 消耗过高
- [#12358](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/issues/12358) — 请求添加普通聊天模式，避免不必要的多任务拆分和工具调用

### Skills 的成功经验

在 Skills 体系中我们已经验证了 **Progressive Disclosure（渐进式披露）** 模式的效果：

```
Phase 1: 注入 skill identifier + description → 轻量元数据
Phase 2: 模型调用 runSkill(name) → 注入完整 skill content + toolset
```

现在将同样的思路应用到 Tools 体系中。

## 方案

### 架构总览

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  PHASE 1: DISCOVERY（发现）                                      │
│                                                                 │
│  注入 <available_tools> 到上下文：                                │
│  - identifier                                                   │
│  - name                                                         │
│  - short description                                            │
│  （每个工具约 50-100 bytes，对比完整 schema 的 2-5KB）             │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                              │
                    模型分析用户请求，
                    判断需要哪些工具
                              │
                              ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  PHASE 2: ACTIVATION（激活）                                     │
│                                                                 │
│  模型调用: activateTools({ identifiers: ["web-browsing",        │
│                               "knowledge-base"] })              │
│                                                                 │
│  系统注入:                                                       │
│  ├── 完整 JSON Schema 加入 tools[]（原生 function calling）      │
│  └── System role 文本注入 system message                         │
│                                                                 │
│  下一次 LLM 调用：已激活工具作为原生 tool calls 可用               │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### 1. 工具发现注入

新增 `ToolDiscoveryProvider`，将轻量级 `<available_tools>` XML 注入上下文：

```xml
<available_tools description="These tools are installed but not yet enabled. Use activateTools to enable them when needed.">
  <tool identifier="lobe-web-browsing" name="Web Browsing">Search the web and browse pages</tool>
  <tool identifier="knowledge-base" name="Knowledge Base">Query your uploaded documents</tool>
  <tool identifier="dalle" name="DALL-E">Generate images from text</tool>
  ...
</available_tools>
```

模型只需要这些元数据就能理解有哪些工具可用，并做出激活决策。

### 2. `activateTools` API

新增 builtin tool `lobe-tools`，提供 `activateTools` 函数：

```typescript
activateTools({ identifiers: ["lobe-web-browsing", "knowledge-base"] })
```

模型被指引：
- **提前规划，在单次调用中激活所有需要的工具**
- 在回复用户之前，分析请求并确定需要的所有工具
- 不要在多步任务中逐步激活

### 3. 动态 Schema 扩展（Re-send 模式）

当 `activateTools` 被调用时：

1. `ToolsActivatorExecutionRuntime` 获取请求工具的完整 manifest
2. 激活的 tool ID 存储到 `stepContext.activatedToolIds`
3. 下一次 LLM 调用时，`createAgentExecutors` 将已激活工具合并到 agent config：
   - 完整 JSON Schema 加入 `tools[]`（原生 function calling）
   - System role 通过 `ToolSystemRoleProvider` 注入
4. 模型现在可以像以前一样使用原生 tool calls

### 4. 累积激活状态

已激活的工具在整个对话中持续有效：
- 通过 `RuntimeStepContext` 中的 `activatedToolIds` 追踪
- 从消息历史中扫描 `lobe-tools` 消息来重建状态
- 一旦激活，工具保持活跃，无需重复激活

### 工具来源

发现系统从所有来源聚合可用工具：

| 来源 | 示例 |
|------|------|
| Builtin tools | Web Browsing、DALL-E、Notebook |
| 用户安装的 plugins | 自定义 MCP servers、社区插件 |
| Klavis MCP servers | 云端 MCP 服务 |
| LobeHub Skills | 基于 Skill 的工具提供者 |

所有来源经过去重后统一呈现在 `<available_tools>` 中。

### UI 集成

新增 `ActivateToolsInspector` 组件提供视觉反馈：
- **激活中**：显示正在激活的工具标识（带闪烁动画）
- **激活完成**：显示工具名称和头像

## Token 节省估算

| 场景 | 优化前（全量） | 优化后（渐进式） | 节省 |
|------|---------------|-----------------|------|
| 20 个工具，使用 3 个 | ~60KB | ~4KB 初始 + ~9KB 激活 = ~13KB | **~78%** |
| 10 个工具，使用 2 个 | ~30KB | ~2KB 初始 + ~6KB 激活 = ~8KB | **~73%** |
| 5 个工具，使用 1 个 | ~15KB | ~1KB 初始 + ~3KB 激活 = ~4KB | **~73%** |

节省量随「已启用但未使用」的工具数量线性增长，这正是配置了大量 MCP server 的 power user 的典型场景。

## 方案对比与取舍

### 为什么选择 Re-send 模式而非 Proxy Tool 模式？

我们评估了三种方案：

| 方案 | 原理 | 优点 | 缺点 |
|------|------|------|------|
| **A. Re-send（采用）** | 激活后重发请求，将 schema 加入 tools[] | 保留原生 function calling 体验 | 需要额外一次 API 调用 |
| B. Proxy Tool | 注册通用 `callTool(id, api, params)` | 无需 re-send | 丢失原生 schema 校验，参数构造易出错 |
| C. 混合模式 | 首轮文本描述 + 下轮原生 calling | 首轮即可使用 | 首次调用不够精确 |

选择 Re-send 的核心原因：**模型在有 typed JSON Schema 时 tool call 准确率显著更高**。多付出一次 API 调用的代价远小于 proxy 模式下参数错误带来的重试开销。

### 延迟影响

激活步骤增加一次 round-trip，但：
- 模型通常在第一次响应中就完成激活，整个对话只多一次调用
- 后续调用因上下文更小，响应速度反而更快
- 指引模型「在单次调用中激活所有工具」来最小化 round-trip

### 向后兼容

- Agent 默认配置中的工具继续正常工作
- 渐进式加载仅对额外可用工具生效
- 现有工具 API 和 manifest 无需任何改动

## 实现状态

已在 PR [#12489](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/pull/12489) 中实现。核心改动：

### 新增
- `packages/prompts/src/prompts/toolDiscovery/` — 可用工具 XML 的 prompt 模板
- `packages/context-engine/src/providers/ToolDiscoveryProvider.ts` — 工具发现上下文注入
- `packages/builtin-tool-tools/src/ExecutionRuntime/` — `activateTools` 执行运行时
- `packages/builtin-tool-tools/src/client/Inspector/ActivateTools/` — 激活反馈 UI 组件

### 改造
- `packages/context-engine/src/engine/messages/MessagesEngine.ts` — Pipeline 集成工具发现
- `packages/types/src/stepContext.ts` — step context 中添加 `activatedToolIds`
- `packages/agent-runtime/src/utils/stepContextComputer.ts` — 从消息历史计算已激活工具
- `src/store/chat/agents/createAgentExecutors.ts` — LLM executor 中动态扩展工具
- `src/store/tool/selectors/tool.ts` — `availableToolsForDiscovery()` selector
- `src/store/chat/slices/message/selectors/dbMessage.ts` — `selectActivatedToolIdsFromMessages()`

## 后续方向

- **智能预加载**：根据对话模式自动激活常用工具
- **工具推荐**：在模型响应前，系统根据用户消息建议相关工具
- **粒度激活**：激活工具内的特定 API，而非整个工具

## 反馈征集

- 这个方案是否符合你的使用场景？
- 有没有需要考虑的边界情况？
- 你更倾向于哪种取舍（例如 Proxy 模式的零延迟激活 vs Re-send 模式的精准调用）？

欢迎在下方评论区分享你的想法！

title: [RFC] 150 - Progressive Tool Loading
body:
## Motivation

### The Problem

When an Agent has many tools enabled (MCP servers, builtin tools, plugins), **all** tool schemas and system prompts are eagerly injected into the context at the start of every conversation:

```
Current behavior (eager loading):
├── tools[] parameter: Full JSON Schema for ALL enabled tools (function calling)
└── system message: ALL tools' systemRole text
```

This creates several real-world pain points:

1. **Context bloat** — Each tool's JSON Schema + system role is ~2-5KB. With 20-30 tools enabled, that's 50-100KB+ of context consumed before the user even sends a message.
2. **Token waste** — Most conversations only use 2-3 tools, yet every request pays the input token cost for all enabled tools.
3. **Degraded quality** — Excessive system context dilutes the model's attention and can reduce response quality.
4. **Cost inefficiency** — Users pay for input tokens on tool schemas they never use.

Community reports:
- [#11915](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/issues/11915) — Users reported excessive token consumption across multiple scenarios
- [#12358](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/issues/12358) — Request to add a plain chat mode to avoid unnecessary tool overhead

### Prior Art: Skills Progressive Disclosure

We've already validated the **Progressive Disclosure** pattern in our Skills system:

```
Phase 1: Inject skill identifier + description → lightweight metadata
Phase 2: Model calls runSkill(name) → inject full skill content + toolset
```

This RFC applies the same approach to the Tools system.

## Design

### Architecture Overview

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  PHASE 1: DISCOVERY                                             │
│                                                                 │
│  Inject <available_tools> into context:                         │
│  - identifier                                                   │
│  - name                                                         │
│  - short description                                            │
│  (~50-100 bytes per tool vs 2-5KB for full schema)              │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                              │
                    Model analyzes user request
                    and determines needed tools
                              │
                              ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  PHASE 2: ACTIVATION                                            │
│                                                                 │
│  Model calls: activateTools({ identifiers: ["web-browsing",     │
│                               "knowledge-base"] })              │
│                                                                 │
│  System injects:                                                │
│  ├── Full JSON Schema into tools[] (native function calling)    │
│  └── System role text into system message                       │
│                                                                 │
│  Next LLM call: activated tools available as native tool calls  │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### 1. Tool Discovery Injection

A new `ToolDiscoveryProvider` injects a lightweight `<available_tools>` XML section into the context:

```xml
<available_tools description="These tools are installed but not yet enabled. Use activateTools to enable them when needed.">
  <tool identifier="lobe-web-browsing" name="Web Browsing">Search the web and browse pages</tool>
  <tool identifier="knowledge-base" name="Knowledge Base">Query your uploaded documents</tool>
  <tool identifier="dalle" name="DALL-E">Generate images from text</tool>
  ...
</available_tools>
```

This is all the model needs to understand what's available and make activation decisions.

### 2. The `activateTools` API

A new builtin tool `lobe-tools` provides the `activateTools` function:

```typescript
activateTools({ identifiers: ["lobe-web-browsing", "knowledge-base"] })
```

The model is instructed to:
- **Plan ahead and activate all needed tools upfront in a single call** — analyze the user's request before responding to determine ALL tools needed
- Do NOT activate tools incrementally during a multi-step task
- Only activate tools that are relevant to the current request

### 3. Dynamic Schema Expansion (Re-send Pattern)

When `activateTools` is called:

1. `ToolsActivatorExecutionRuntime` fetches the full manifests for requested tools
2. Activated tool IDs are stored in `stepContext.activatedToolIds`
3. On the next LLM call, `createAgentExecutors` merges activated tools into the agent config:
   - Full JSON Schema added to `tools[]` for native function calling
   - System roles injected via `ToolSystemRoleProvider`
4. The model can now call activated tools with the exact same native experience as before

### 4. Cumulative Activation State

Activated tools persist for the entire conversation:
- Tracked via `activatedToolIds` in `RuntimeStepContext`
- Reconstructed from message history by scanning `lobe-tools` messages
- Once activated, a tool stays active — no need to re-activate

### Tool Sources

The discovery system aggregates available tools from all sources:

| Source | Examples |
|--------|----------|
| Builtin tools | Web Browsing, DALL-E, Notebook |
| User-installed plugins | Custom MCP servers, community plugins |
| Klavis MCP servers | Cloud MCP services |
| LobeHub Skills | Skill-based tool providers |

All sources are deduplicated and presented uniformly in the `<available_tools>` section.

### UI Integration

A new `ActivateToolsInspector` component provides visual feedback:
- **During activation**: Shows which tools are being activated (with shimmer animation)
- **After activation**: Displays activated tool names with avatars

## Estimated Token Savings

| Scenario | Before (Eager) | After (Progressive) | Savings |
|----------|----------------|---------------------|---------|
| 20 tools, use 3 | ~60KB | ~4KB initial + ~9KB activated = ~13KB | **~78%** |
| 10 tools, use 2 | ~30KB | ~2KB initial + ~6KB activated = ~8KB | **~73%** |
| 5 tools, use 1 | ~15KB | ~1KB initial + ~3KB activated = ~4KB | **~73%** |

Savings scale with the number of enabled-but-unused tools — exactly the common case for power users with many MCP servers configured.

## Alternatives Considered

| Approach | How it works | Pros | Cons |
|----------|-------------|------|------|
| **A. Re-send (chosen)** | After activation, re-send request with schema in tools[] | Preserves native function calling | One extra API round-trip |
| B. Proxy Tool | Register a generic `callTool(id, api, params)` | No re-send needed | Loses native schema validation; model must construct params from memory |
| C. Hybrid | First turn uses text description; next turn gets native calling | Usable immediately | First call may be imprecise |

We chose Re-send because **models perform significantly better with typed JSON Schemas for tool parameters**. The cost of one extra API call is far less than the retry overhead from parameter errors in a proxy pattern.

### Latency Impact

The activation step adds one round-trip, but:
- The model typically activates tools in its first response, so the overhead is a single extra call per conversation
- Reduced context size can actually speed up subsequent calls
- The "activate all tools upfront in a single call" instruction minimizes round-trips

### Backward Compatibility

- Tools in the agent's default configuration continue to work unchanged
- Progressive loading only applies to additional available tools
- No changes to existing tool APIs or manifests

## Implementation

Implemented in PR [#12489](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/pull/12489). Key changes:

### New
- `packages/prompts/src/prompts/toolDiscovery/` — Prompt templates for available tools XML
- `packages/context-engine/src/providers/ToolDiscoveryProvider.ts` — Context provider for tool discovery injection
- `packages/builtin-tool-tools/src/ExecutionRuntime/` — `activateTools` execution runtime
- `packages/builtin-tool-tools/src/client/Inspector/ActivateTools/` — UI component for activation feedback

### Modified
- `packages/context-engine/src/engine/messages/MessagesEngine.ts` — Pipeline integration for tool discovery
- `packages/types/src/stepContext.ts` — Added `activatedToolIds` to step context
- `packages/agent-runtime/src/utils/stepContextComputer.ts` — Compute activated tools from message history
- `src/store/chat/agents/createAgentExecutors.ts` — Dynamic tool expansion in LLM executor
- `src/store/tool/selectors/tool.ts` — `availableToolsForDiscovery()` selector
- `src/store/chat/slices/message/selectors/dbMessage.ts` — `selectActivatedToolIdsFromMessages()`

## Future Directions

- **Smart preloading** — Automatically activate commonly-used tools based on conversation patterns
- **Tool recommendation** — System suggests relevant tools based on user message before the model responds
- **Granular activation** — Activate specific APIs within a tool rather than the entire tool

## Feedback Welcome

- Does this approach align with your usage patterns?
- Are there edge cases we should consider?
- Would you prefer different trade-offs (e.g., proxy pattern for zero-latency activation)?

Share your thoughts in the comments below!

title: [RFC] 151 - IM Bot Integration: Deploy Any Agent as Discord / Slack Bot
body:
## Background

LobeHub is a Web-centric AI Agent platform. Agents created in LobeHub can only be used through the web UI. However, many teams already rely on Discord, Slack, Feishu and other IM platforms for daily collaboration.

**Core goal: allow any Agent built in LobeHub to be deployed as an IM Bot with one click, so it can be @mentioned and used directly in Discord / Slack / etc.** — similar to projects like [OpenClaw](https://openclaw.com), extending AI Agents from the web into the collaboration spaces where users already live.

This means:
- An Agent's full capabilities (System Prompt, tools, knowledge base, model config) are directly consumable by IM Bots
- Multi-step reasoning and tool calls show clear real-time progress in the IM channel
- Multi-turn conversations are supported via threads, with context automatically maintained
- A Provider-based architecture enables unified integration across Discord, Slack, and future platforms

## Architecture Overview

```
                    ┌─ /api/agent/webhooks/discord  ─┐
Discord User ──→   │                                 │
                    │                                 ↓
Slack User   ──→   ├─ /api/agent/webhooks/slack    ──→  BotMessageRouter
                    │                                 ↑   (Chat SDK message routing)
Feishu User  ──→   ├─ /api/agent/webhooks/feishu   ──┘        │
                    │                                          ↓
                    │                              AgentBridgeService
                    │                          (platform-agnostic bridge)
                    │                                          │
                    │                                          ↓
                    │                              AiAgentService.execAgent()
                    │                                          │
                    └──────────────────────────────────── Agent Runtime
```

### Core Layers

| Layer | Component | Responsibility |
|-------|-----------|---------------|
| **Webhook** | `/api/agent/webhooks/[platform]` | Receives platform webhooks, delegates to router |
| **Routing** | `BotMessageRouter` | Unified message event handling via Chat SDK, manages bot instance pool |
| **Bridge** | `AgentBridgeService` | Platform-agnostic Agent execution bridge, manages message lifecycle |
| **Runtime** | `AiAgentService` → `AgentRuntime` | Existing Agent execution engine (LLM + tool calls + multi-step reasoning) |
| **Gateway** | `GatewayManager` | Bot instance lifecycle management, auto-discovery and start/stop |
| **Storage** | `agentBotProviders` table | Per-agent bot config persistence with encrypted credentials |
| **UI** | Agent Integration Page | Bot Provider management UI in Agent settings |

## Detailed Design

### 1. Per-Agent Bot Provider

Each Agent can independently configure its own Bot Providers, decoupled from any global config:

- A `agent_bot_providers` table stores platform, application ID, and encrypted credentials per agent
- Webhook routing: incoming webhook → extract `applicationId` → look up which agent owns it → execute with that agent's config
- Unique constraint on `(platform, application_id)` ensures fast webhook-to-agent resolution

### 2. BotMessageRouter

Built on [Chat SDK](https://github.com/nicepkg/chat), providing unified message event handling:

- **@mention handling**: Detects @Bot messages → creates Thread → delegates to AgentBridgeService
- **Thread tracking**: Auto-subscribes to replied threads; follow-up messages continue as multi-turn conversation
- **Bot instance pool**: Maintains Chat SDK instances keyed by `applicationId`, supporting multiple bots in parallel

### 3. AgentBridgeService

The core hub that converts Chat SDK message events into Agent executions:

**Message lifecycle:**

1. Message received → add 👀 reaction (acknowledged)
2. Post initial progress message (randomized ack phrase)
3. Agent executes → edit progress message at each step with real-time status
4. Execution complete → edit into final reply with usage footer
5. Remove 👀 reaction (done)

### 4. Real-time Progress Display

Inspired by Claude Code's output style, providing clear tool call progress:

```
○ builtin·web_search(query: "latest news")       ← LLM decided to call (hollow circle, pending)

⏺ builtin·web_search(query: "latest news")       ← Tool execution complete (filled circle)
  ⎿  Found 3 results about...                     ← Result summary

⏺ lobe-web-browsing·readUrl(url: "https://...")
  ⎿  Page loaded successfully … +12 lines
```

Final reply includes usage stats:

```
Here is the answer based on my research...

---
**1.2k** tokens · $0.0312 | llm×5 | tools×4
```

### 5. Non-streaming LLM Mode

Bot scenarios don't need token-by-token streaming (IM messages are posted as complete replies). A `stream: false` option is added to `execAgent()`, allowing the LLM to return a complete response in one shot, reducing overhead.

### 6. GatewayManager

Manages the lifecycle of all bot instances:

- **Auto-discovery**: Loads all enabled bot providers from DB on startup
- **On-demand start/stop**: Individual bot start/stop support
- **Credential security**: Encrypted storage and decryption via KeyVaultsGateKeeper

### 7. Agent Integration Page

A new **Integration** tab in Agent settings:

- View configured Bot Providers
- Add new Bot Provider (select platform → enter credentials)
- One-click connect / disconnect
- Enable / disable / delete providers

## Platform Support

| Platform | Status | Adapter |
|----------|--------|---------|
| Discord | ✅ Implemented | `@chat-adapter/discord` |
| Slack | 🔜 Planned | `@chat-adapter/slack` |
| Feishu | 🔜 Planned | TBD |
| Microsoft Teams | 📋 Future | TBD |

Adding a new platform requires only:
1. Implement the `PlatformBot` interface
2. Register the adapter in GatewayManager
3. Add a webhook handler in BotMessageRouter

## Future Work

- **Slack / Feishu / Teams adapters** — reuse the same Bridge architecture
- **Message attachments** — support images, files, and rich media
- **Slash commands** — trigger specific tools via Bot slash commands
- **Bot marketplace** — one-click publish an Agent as an installable IM Bot
- **Rate limiting & abuse protection** — per-bot rate limits
- **Analytics dashboard** — bot usage, token consumption metrics

title: [RFC] 152 - (WIP)Supporting MoltBook-Style Background Tasks via Scheduled Task + Credentials Built-in Tools
body:
## 1. Summary The primary scope of this RFC is to support MoltBook-like task patterns that require both recurring background execution and credential management, by integrating two new built-in tools. Core changes: 1. Add `lobe-scheduled-task` to handle cron task operations (`set/get/delete/list`). 2. Add `lobe-credentials` as a read-first built-in tool (`list/get`) for credential discovery and safe reference; prioritize deterministic credential UI for write/update/rotation. 3. Integrate credential injection and missing-credential guidance into the `lobe-cloud-sandbox` execution path. 4. Provide a minimal dispatcher trigger endpoint (`/api/agent/cron/dispatch`) as supporting capability for end-to-end automation. The goal is to provide practical, controllable, and reusable task orchestration for MoltBook-style agent workflows. ## 2. Background and Problem MoltBook is positioned as a **social network for AI agents**. Agents are expected to operate continuously as community participants (posting, commenting, engaging), not via one-off API calls. Based on MoltBook `skill.md`, integration naturally requires: 1. Long-lived identity credential management: after registration, agents call APIs via `Authorization: Bearer `, and key rotation must be supported. 2. Periodic background execution: heartbeat-style recurring checks (example: every 30 minutes). 3. Stable execution with strict security boundary: requests must go to `https://www.moltbook.com`, and API keys must only be sent to authorized domain targets. Mapped to LobeHub, MoltBook-style tasks require: 1. In-chat task lifecycle management (`set/get/delete/list`). 2. Secure credential retrieval, storage, update/rotation, and reuse. 3. Safe runtime credential consumption without repeatedly exposing plaintext in chat context. 4. A self-hosting execution loop that can actually trigger tasks. Before this branch, key gaps were: 1. No dedicated task-management tool path for agent-side operations. 2. No dedicated credential-management tool path for agent-side operations. 3. No standardized sandbox credential injection path, causing plaintext leakage risk in prompts/commands. 4. No self-hosting dispatch trigger loop for true automation closure. Therefore, MoltBook is not an occasional API-use case. It is a representative scenario of recurring execution + sensitive credential management + strict domain boundary, which directly motivates this RFC scope. ## 3. Goals and Non-goals ### 3.1 Goals 1. Integrate `lobe-scheduled-task` so agents can set/get/delete/list scheduled tasks in chat. 2. Integrate `lobe-credentials` so agents can reliably discover/retrieve keyVault credentials in chat, while write/update/rotation is primarily handled by deterministic UI. 3. Close the credential execution path: `Credentials -> keyVaults -> Cloud Sandbox.runCommand`. 4. Deliver an executable closed loop for MoltBook-style workloads (task definition + secret management + recurring trigger + execution). 5. Ensure self-hosting can run this flow with minimal supporting dispatch capability. ### 3.2 Non-goals 1. Do not design a brand-new generic scheduler or queue architecture in this RFC. 2. Do not support advanced schedule semantics (second-level precision, DAG dependencies, multi-stage workflows). 3. For `lobe-credentials`, do not introduce an independent secret storage system. Reuse existing keyVaults data model and the `user_settings.key_vaults` field (`packages/database/src/schemas/user.ts`) without schema/table redesign. 4. For `lobe-scheduled-task`, continue reusing existing `agentCronJob` data model and `agent_cron_jobs` table (`packages/database/src/schemas/agentCronJob.ts`) without schema/table redesign. ### 3.3 Scope Boundary 1. In scope: two built-in tools, Cloud Sandbox credential consumption, minimal dispatch closure. 2. Supporting scope: dispatcher API, sidecar scheduler, runtime tuning, health checks. 3. Out of scope: context management for sessions spawned by cron tasks (e.g., autonomous social context handling), advanced orchestration platform, cross-tenant scheduling governance, complex resource scheduling strategy. ## 4. Solution Overview ### 4.1 Architecture This RFC focuses on this capability chain: `Scheduled Task Tool` (task lifecycle) + `Credentials Tool` (secrets) + `Cloud Sandbox` (execution/injection) + `Dispatcher Tick` (supporting trigger) ```mermaid flowchart LR U["User / Reviewer"] --> A["Agent (LLM)"] A --> ST["lobe-scheduled-task"] A --> CR["lobe-credentials"] A --> CS["lobe-cloud-sandbox.runCommand"] ST --> DB1["agent_cron_jobs"] CR --> DB2["user_settings.key_vaults"] SC["Deploy curl sidecar
cron-dispatcher"] --> D["POST /api/agent/cron/dispatch"] D --> DISP["AgentCronDispatcher"] DISP --> EX["AiAgentService.execAgent(trigger='cron')"] EX --> CS CS --> MB["moltbook.com APIs"] ``` Responsibilities: 1. `scheduled-task runtime`: business-level `set/get/delete/list` handling and validation for cron jobs. 2. `credentials runtime`: path-based keyVault read/write with masked output. 3. `cloud sandbox runtime`: execute `runCommand` and inject keyVault-derived env values. 4. `AgentCronDispatcher` (supporting): due-job scan, idempotent trigger, and dispatch stats. ### 4.2 Scheduled Task Tool Integration (Primary Scope) New package: `@lobechat/builtin-tool-scheduled-task` ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant U as User participant A as Agent participant T as lobe-scheduled-task participant R as scheduledTask runtime participant M as AgentCronJobModel participant DB as agent_cron_jobs U->>A: "Create heartbeat every 30 minutes" A->>T: setScheduledTask(...) T-->>A: humanIntervention required U->>A: confirm A->>R: execute set (create path) R->>R: normalize + validate cronPattern/timezone/maxExecutions R->>M: create job M->>DB: INSERT DB-->>M: jobId M-->>R: created record R-->>A: BuiltinServerRuntimeOutput(success/state) ``` #### Manifest (API Parameter Summary) 1. `setScheduledTask` (`humanIntervention: required`) - Create path (`jobId` omitted): requires `name`, `content`, `cronPattern` - Update path (`jobId` provided): requires `jobId` + at least one mutable field - Optional: `agentId`, `description`, `enabled`, `maxExecutions`, `timezone` 2. `getScheduledTask` - Required: `jobId` 3. `deleteScheduledTask` (`humanIntervention: required`) - Required: `jobId` 4. `listScheduledTasks` - Optional: `agentId`, `enabled`, `limit`, `offset` #### Notes 1. `set/delete` are gated by `humanIntervention: required`; `get/list` are not. 2. `maxExecutions` supports `number | null` (no magic value for unlimited runs). #### Runtime Normalization and Validation 1. Normalize `maxExecutions` (supports integer-like strings and `null`) and validate range `1..10000`. 2. Backfill `agentId` from context; fail if no target agent is available. 3. Default `timezone` to `UTC`. 4. For `setScheduledTask` update path, require at least one mutable field. 5. In server runtime, apply `validateCronPatternByDeployment` for `setScheduledTask` create/update paths. #### System Prompt and Human Intervention 1. Prompt requires explicit confirmation before set/delete. 2. If `jobId` is missing for set update path/delete, list tasks first. 3. Keep task `content` as single-run execution instruction (no schedule cadence in content). #### Return Contract and UI Behavior 1. Return unified `BuiltinServerRuntimeOutput` (`success/content/state`), with `state` including fields such as `jobId`, `cronPattern`, `enabled`, `maxExecutions`, `timezone`, `updatedFields`. 2. On success, trigger `cronTopicsWithJobInfo` SWR mutate to refresh sidebar/task views. #### Database and Existing Infrastructure Integration 1. Reuse existing table `agent_cron_jobs` (`packages/database/src/schemas/agentCronJob.ts`). 2. Reuse existing `AgentCronJobModel` for scheduled-task persistence/pagination/execution stats (`packages/database/src/models/agentCronJob.ts`). 3. Reuse existing cron router/service paths. #### Scheme Comparison (Feasible Options Only) Definition: 1. A: add `lobe-scheduled-task` and reuse `agent_cron_jobs` + `AgentCronJobModel` | Scheme | Change Complexity | Forward Compatibility | Backward Compatibility | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | A (Current) | Medium: new tool + runtime adaptation, no DB migration | High: centralized schema/runtime validation allows smooth extension | High: reuses existing table/model with no breakage to current task data | #### Integration Points 1. Built-in tool registry (`identifier/defaultToolIds/builtinTools`). 2. Frontend built-in executors. 3. Server runtimes (bound to `AgentCronJobModel`). #### Supporting Capability Changes 1. Remove `enableBusinessFeatures` gating from scheduled-task related pages. 2. Add `custom` mode in cron config UI for raw cron expression input. 3. Remove front-end forced minute normalization to `0/30`. 4. In `packages/types`, relax `minimumIntervalSchema` to `cronPatternSchema`. #### Policy, Compatibility, and Risk 1. Add `agentCronPolicy`: enforce minimum 30-minute interval in cloud mode (`VERCEL=1`). 2. Current `setScheduledTask` create/update paths in server runtime already use this policy. 3. Existing task data remains compatible (`cronPattern` is still standard 5-field cron). 4. Risk: policy consistency across all cron write paths. 5. Mitigation: unify validation usage across all write entries. ### 4.3 Credentials Tool Integration (Primary Scope) New package: `@lobechat/builtin-tool-credentials` ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant U as User participant A as Agent participant T as lobe-credentials participant R as credentials runtime participant UM as UserModel participant KV as user_settings.key_vaults U->>A: "Store MoltBook API key" A->>T: setCredential(path="moltbook.apiKey", value="...") T-->>A: humanIntervention required U->>A: confirm T->>R: execute setCredential R->>UM: updateSetting(key_vaults) UM->>KV: encrypted write KV-->>R: ok R-->>A: success + masked state U->>A: "Check credential path and usage" A->>T: listCredentials(prefix="moltbook.") T->>R: execute listCredentials R->>UM: getUserSettings UM->>KV: encrypted read KV-->>R: decrypted values R-->>A: masked result + path hints A->>T: getCredential(path="moltbook.apiKey", reveal=false) T->>R: execute getCredential(reveal=false) R->>UM: getUserSettings UM->>KV: encrypted read KV-->>R: decrypted value R-->>A: valueMasked ``` #### Manifest (API Parameter Summary) 1. `setCredential` (`humanIntervention: required`) - Required: `path`, `value` 2. `listCredentials` - Optional: `prefix` 3. `getCredential` (`humanIntervention: required`) - Required: `path` - Optional: `reveal` 4. `deleteCredential` (`humanIntervention: required`) - Required: `path` #### Notes 1. Current implementation includes full CRUD (`set/get/list/delete`) and the operational flow commonly uses `setCredential`. 2. `additionalProperties: false` is used to reduce malformed/hallucinated input payloads. #### Runtime Normalization and Validation 1. Normalize and validate `path` format. 2. `getCredential` is masked by default; plaintext only with explicit `reveal=true`. #### System Prompt and Human Intervention 1. Prompt enforces masked-by-default secret handling and discourages plaintext reveal unless explicitly requested. 2. Prompt prefers service-scoped keys (e.g., `moltbook.apiKey`) as the primary matching path, with `sandboxEnv.` kept as compatibility fallback. 3. Prompt allows `setCredential` for onboarding/rotation (with confirmation) and still encourages `listCredentials/getCredential` for path discovery. #### Return Contract and UI Behavior 1. Return unified `BuiltinServerRuntimeOutput` with structured `state` fields (`path/valueMasked/paths/items/deleted/exists`, etc.). 2. `getCredential` is masked by default and returns plaintext only with explicit `reveal=true`. #### UI Management Capability (Implemented) 1. `lobe-credentials` manual-management UI is implemented with explicit `list/set/update/delete`. 2. UI is masked-by-default, with controlled reveal/hide flow and rotation guidance. 3. UI supports prefix filtering for service-scoped credential management. 4. UI and tool writes share the same keyVaults storage and refresh user state after persistence, so updates are immediately consumable. #### Database and Existing Infrastructure Integration 1. Reuse `user_settings.key_vaults` (`packages/database/src/schemas/user.ts`). 2. Reuse `UserModel.getUserSettings/updateSetting` (`packages/database/src/models/user.ts`). 3. Reuse `KeyVaultsGateKeeper` for encryption/decryption (`src/server/modules/KeyVaultsEncrypt/index.ts`). #### Scheme Comparison (Feasible Options) Definition: 1. A: UI-first write/update/delete + read-first tool (`list/get`) on existing `keyVaults` 2. B: full CRUD by tool (`set/get/list/delete`) on existing `keyVaults` | Scheme | Change Complexity | Forward Compatibility | Backward Compatibility | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | A (Preferred) | Low-medium: add read runtime + UI operations, no DB migration | High: deterministic writes + reusable read contract reduce LLM/tool coupling | High: fully reuses existing encrypted keyVault data and paths | | B (Alternative) | Medium: simpler UX surface initially, but higher tool-path complexity | Medium: write success depends more on tool-call quality and intervention flow | High: no DB/storage migration needed | #### Design Rationale (UI-first + Minimal Tool Baseline) 1. The design uses a dual track for reliability and flexibility: deterministic writes in UI, programmable calls in tools. 2. Runtime execution closure is kept in `lobe-cloud-sandbox` (service-key mapping + env injection), so LLM does not need plaintext secrets in chat context. 3. Reusing existing `keyVaults` schema and encryption chain keeps integration risk low and avoids new storage complexity. #### Baseline and Enablement Strategy 1. Keep the minimal-change tool baseline as `listCredentials + getCredential`. 2. `setCredential/deleteCredential` remain implemented and can be enabled by scenario. #### Added Tests 1. No DB migration is required. 2. Added execution runtime tests for both `scheduled-task` and `credentials`. ### 4.4 Credentials × Cloud Sandbox Execution Path (Primary Scope) #### System Prompt Changes `lobe-cloud-sandbox` prompt is enhanced for credentials collaboration: 1. Add credentials capabilities (`setCredential/getCredential/listCredentials/deleteCredential`) into capability set. 2. Add workflow rule: use credentials on demand (no unnecessary pre-check calls). 3. Add security rule: do not use `reveal=true` unless explicitly requested. 4. Add missing-secret handling: if runtime reports missing env vars, guide to `setCredential(path=".", value="...")` first (e.g., `moltbook.apiKey`), and use `sandboxEnv.` as compatibility fallback. 5. Add output rule: do not expose plaintext secrets in normal responses. ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant U as User participant A as Agent participant C as lobe-credentials participant KV as keyVaults (encrypted) participant S as lobe-cloud-sandbox runtime participant X as Sandbox Executor participant API as External API (moltbook.com) U->>A: provide/rotate MoltBook API key A->>C: setCredential(path="moltbook.apiKey", value="...") C->>KV: encrypted write A->>C: listCredentials(prefix="moltbook.") C->>KV: encrypted read A->>S: runCommand("curl ... -H 'Authorization: Bearer $MOLTBOOK_API_KEY'") S->>KV: load credentials S->>S: map moltbook.apiKey -> MOLTBOOK_API_KEY S->>X: execute with injected env X->>API: authenticated request X-->>S: execution result S-->>A: redacted logs + safe output ``` #### Runtime/Executor Changes in `lobe-cloud-sandbox` 1. Build env candidates from user keyVaults. 2. Inject only when `runCommand` references `$ENV` variables. 3. Fast-fail missing credential-like env names with actionable `setCredential` guidance (or credentials-UI guidance in minimal-change deployments). 4. Redact command body in logs. 5. Add stable mapping from service-scoped keys to env names (e.g., `moltbook.apiKey -> MOLTBOOK_API_KEY`) with matching priority `service. > sandboxEnv.`. #### Existing Infrastructure Integration 1. keyVault read path remains `UserModel + KeyVaultsGateKeeper`. 2. execution remains via existing `ServerSandboxService + MarketService`. 3. cron-triggered execution remains via existing `AiAgentService.execAgent` (dispatcher is supporting layer). #### Scheme Comparison (Feasible Options Only) Definition: 1. A: runtime auto-injects env vars during `runCommand`, with credentials UI as primary write path 2. B: runtime auto-injects env vars during `runCommand`, with tool CRUD (`set/get/list/delete`) as primary write path | Scheme | Change Complexity | Semantic Consistency | Backward Compatibility | Task Reliability | Security | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | A (Preferred) | Medium: runtime mapping/injection + deterministic UI flows | High: write path is deterministic, read path remains tool-friendly | High: no DB write-path change | High | High | | B (Alternative) | Medium: fewer UI dependencies, more tool mutation handling | Medium: mutation quality depends on LLM + intervention flow | High: no DB write-path change | Medium | High | #### Decision 1. For MoltBook (recurring, high-frequency, strict key boundary), prioritize security and reuse. 2. Keep current implemented write path (`setCredential`) explicit, while preserving the minimal-change option (`list/get` + UI write path). 3. Keep runtime env mapping/injection as the stable execution baseline. #### Stable Execution Path for MoltBook 1. Store/update credentials via `setCredential` in the current implementation (prefer `moltbook.apiKey`, fallback compatible `sandboxEnv.MOLTBOOK_API_KEY`), and ToolUI manager remains available as the deterministic write path. 2. Let scheduled execution inject env vars automatically in sandbox runtime. 3. Use `listCredentials/getCredential` so LLM can reference the correct variable path without carrying plaintext secrets in task content. #### Security and Privacy (Integrated) 1. Credentials are masked by default. 2. Cloud Sandbox logs use redacted command output (`[REDACTED_COMMAND]` + metadata). 3. Missing env vars fail explicitly to avoid unauthenticated external calls. #### Testing and Acceptance (Integrated) 1. Added sandbox tests for env injection/matching priority, missing-secret blocking, and non-`runCommand` isolation. 2. Recommended check: when `$MOLTBOOK_API_KEY` is missing, runtime returns actionable repair guidance. 3. Recommended check: when both paths exist, `moltbook.apiKey` mapping is matched first and `sandboxEnv.MOLTBOOK_API_KEY` remains fallback-compatible. ### 4.5 Dispatcher API (Supporting Scope) New endpoint: `POST /api/agent/cron/dispatch` Auth (either): 1. QStash signature (`QSTASH_CURRENT_SIGNING_KEY` + `QSTASH_NEXT_SIGNING_KEY`) 2. Bearer token (`AGENT_CRON_DISPATCH_API_KEY`) Body: 1. `dryRun?: boolean` 2. `now?: ISO datetime` 3. `maxJobsPerTick?: number` Response includes: 1. `tickAt` 2. `jobs[]` (`triggered/skipped/failed`) 3. `stats` (`scanned/eligible/triggered/skipped/failed/durationMs`) Health check: `GET /api/agent/cron/dispatch` #### Self-hosting Runtime and Deployment (Integrated) New env vars: 1. `AGENT_CRON_DISPATCH_API_KEY` 2. `AGENT_CRON_DISPATCH_MAX_JOBS_PER_TICK` 3. `AGENT_CRON_DISPATCH_CONCURRENCY` New Docker sidecar: 1. `docker-compose/deploy` includes `cron-dispatcher` (POST every 60s). 2. `docker-compose/dev` provides optional `--profile cron` sidecar. 3. `package.json` includes `dev:docker:cron` helper script. Compatibility and risk: 1. Without a scheduler trigger in self-hosting, tasks remain configurable but won’t auto-run. 2. Risk: sidecar misconfiguration can silently prevent triggers. 3. Mitigation: add `GET /api/agent/cron/dispatch` + `dryRun` checks to deployment checklist. ### 4.6 Dispatch Evaluation and Idempotency (Supporting Scope) Per dispatch tick, `AgentCronDispatcher`: 1. Loads enabled jobs (bounded by `maxJobsPerTick`). 2. Evaluates due jobs by `cronPattern + timezone + executionConditions + lastExecutedAt`. 3. Acquires idempotency lock key: `cron:job:{jobId}:slot:{YYYYMMDDHHmm}`. 4. Triggers execution via `AiAgentService.execAgent(... trigger='cron', cronJobId=...)`. 5. Updates execution stats after successful trigger. Lock strategy: 1. Prefer Redis (`SET NX EX`). 2. Fallback to in-memory lock when Redis is unavailable (local/dev use). Both tools are `hidden: true` by default but callable by the agent. #### Observability, Testing, and Risk (Integrated) New debug namespaces: 1. `lobe-server:agent-cron-dispatcher` 2. `api-route:agent:cron-dispatch` 3. enhanced sandbox logs under `lobe-server:sandbox-service` Core metrics: 1. Tick-level: `scanned/triggered/skipped/failed/durationMs` 2. Job-level: `jobId/operationId/skipReason` Added coverage: 1. `agentCronDispatcher`: cron matching, timezone handling, slot de-duplication, evalContext extraction 2. `dispatch route`: `401/400/200`, auth probing, input parsing 3. `agentCronPolicy`: cloud vs self-host policy behavior Recommended acceptance: 1. Create a `*/30 * * * *` task and trigger dispatch. 2. Repeated dispatch within same minute does not double-trigger same job. Compatibility and risk: 1. Works without Redis, but idempotency is process-local (multi-replica risk). 2. Risk: in-memory lock cannot prevent duplicates across replicas. 3. Mitigation: require Redis in production and monitor lock hit rate. ## 5. MoltBook User Story (Post-integration) For MoltBook, user-visible flow is split into three chains: onboarding, heartbeat (background), and foreground chat operations. Onboarding chain: ```mermaid flowchart LR OB1["Import + run MoltBook skill"] --> OB2["Obtain API key via sandbox"] OB2 --> OB3["setCredential(moltbook.apiKey)"] OB3 --> OB4["setScheduledTask(heartbeat)"] OB4 --> OB5["Human manual claim"] ``` Heartbeat (background) chain: ```mermaid flowchart LR BG1["Dispatcher tick"] --> BG2["Cron context execAgent"] BG2 --> BG3["runCommand with auto-injected key"] BG3 --> BG4["DM actions blocked in headless mode"] BG4 --> BG5["Pending DM intent surfaced to foreground"] ``` Foreground chat chain: ```mermaid flowchart LR FG1["User requests post/reply/DM"] --> FG2["runCommand with injected key"] FG2 --> FG3["Key rotation via setCredential"] FG3 --> FG4["Heartbeat adjustments via setScheduledTask"] ``` ### 5.1 Onboarding Chain 1. User asks the agent to read `https://www.moltbook.com/skill.md` and join MoltBook. Agent triggers `lobe-skill-store.importSkill`, then persists the skill. 2. Agent activates the skill via `lobe-skill.runSkill` and follows onboarding steps. 3. During onboarding, agent runs `lobe-cloud-sandbox.runCommand` to obtain MoltBook API key and stores/updates it via `lobe-credentials.setCredential` (match `moltbook.apiKey` first, keep `sandboxEnv.MOLTBOOK_API_KEY` as compatible fallback). In minimal-change deployments, this write can be handled by credentials UI. 4. Before creating the recurring task, agent reads `heartbeat.md` via `lobe-skill.readReference` to get recommended heartbeat behavior/schedule. 5. Agent calls `lobe-scheduled-task.setScheduledTask` to create heartbeat job. 6. Agent asks human to complete manual claim on MoltBook. ### 5.2 Heartbeat (Background Task) Chain 1. Dispatcher triggers at cron window and enters scheduled execution context. 2. Agent executes heartbeat logic through `lobe-cloud-sandbox.runCommand`; runtime auto-injects `MOLTBOOK_API_KEY` (service-path mapping first, `sandboxEnv.*` fallback-compatible). 3. DM actions require explicit human approval per MoltBook skill guidance. Since scheduled jobs run with `humanIntervention=headless`, DM actions are not auto-processed in background; agent surfaces pending DM intent for user approval in foreground chat. ### 5.3 Foreground Chat Chain 1. In foreground chat, user can request real-time operations (post/reply/notifications/DM). Agent executes via `lobe-cloud-sandbox.runCommand` with injected credentials. 2. If key is expired or rotated, agent updates it via `lobe-credentials.setCredential` (minimal-change deployments may handle write/update in credentials UI). 3. If heartbeat strategy changes, agent adjusts via `lobe-scheduled-task.setScheduledTask`. ## 6. Key Changes ### 6.1 Two New Built-in Tool Integrations (Primary) 1. Add `lobe-scheduled-task` and `lobe-credentials`. 2. Complete manifest, execution runtime, executor, identifier, and locale integration. 3. Keep both tools hidden by default as background capability tools. ### 6.2 Closed Loop for MoltBook-style Workloads (Primary) 1. `lobe-credentials.setCredential` (implemented) manages API key/token write/update in keyVaults. 2. `lobe-scheduled-task` manages cron lifecycle via `set/get/delete/list`. 3. `lobe-credentials` (`list/get`) helps LLM discover and reference valid credential paths. 4. `lobe-cloud-sandbox` consumes credentials automatically and guides repair on missing secrets. 5. Forms a reusable chain: recurring task + secret management + script execution. ## 7. Release Plan (Suggested) 1. Phase 1 (done): ship credentials manual-management UI + runtime mapping/injection baseline. 2. Phase 2 (done): switch scheduled-task APIs to `set/get/delete/list` and complete credentials tool/UI linkage. 3. Phase 3: verify end-to-end MoltBook closure (injection, dispatch, execution) and unify cron policy validation across write paths. ## 8. Change List (Core Files) 1. Builtin Tools: - `packages/builtin-tool-scheduled-task/*` - `packages/builtin-tool-credentials/*` - `packages/builtin-tools/src/*` 2. Tool Runtime: - `src/server/services/toolExecution/serverRuntimes/scheduledTask.ts` - `src/server/services/toolExecution/serverRuntimes/credentials.ts` - `src/server/services/toolExecution/serverRuntimes/cloudSandbox.ts` 3. Cron UI: - `src/routes/(main)/agent/cron/[cronId]/*` - `src/routes/(main)/agent/profile/features/*` - `src/routes/(main)/agent/_layout/Sidebar/Cron/index.tsx` 4. Dispatcher (supporting): - `src/server/services/agentCronDispatcher/*` - `src/app/(backend)/api/agent/cron/dispatch/route.ts` 5. Env & Deployment (supporting): - `.env.example*` - `docker-compose/dev/*` - `docker-compose/deploy/*` - `docs/self-hosting/environment-variables/basic*.mdx` ## 9. Open Questions ### 9.1 Open Questions for Review 1. Tool-result readability for LLM: how should `lobe-scheduled-task` and `lobe-credentials` structure error/result payloads so the model can more reliably diagnose, recover, and choose next actions? 2. UI presentation quality: with credentials ToolUI manager already online, what focused UX refinements are still needed for validation/human-intervention/repair-hint visibility? 3. MoltBook heartbeat context management: what context model (windowing, summary state, retry context, dedupe keys) should be used so long-running heartbeat jobs remain stable without context drift?

title: [Feature Proposal] Conditional Agent Pipelines — Multi-agent workflows with routing and feedback loops
body:
## Overview

LobeHub's Agent Groups feature is a great foundation for multi-agent collaboration. I'd like to propose taking it further: **Conditional Agent Pipelines** a way to define stateful, multi-agent workflows where agents hand off tasks to each other based on conditions, with support for feedback loops and re-routing.

Think of it as LangGraph-style state machines, but built natively into LobeHub's UI.

## The Problem

Right now, if I want to run a complex agentic workflow (say, research, plan, build, review) I have to:
- Do it manually, copy-pasting context between agent sessions
- Use an external tool (LangGraph, CrewAI, AutoGen) and lose LobeHub's excellent UI
- Hope each agent "remembers" the prior context correctly

There's no way to define a pipeline once and have LobeHub execute it autonomously with conditional routing.

## The Solution: Agent Pipelines

A **Pipeline** is a directed graph of agents where:
- Each **node** is a specialized agent with a role (Scout, Planner, Builder, Reviewer, etc.)
- Each **edge** is a handoff with optional conditions (`on_success`, `on_error`, `on_review_failed`, etc.)
- **Context flows forward** automatically, each agent receives prior agents outputs
- **Feedback loops** are supported. Reviewer can route back to Builder or Planner

### Example: Scout, Planner, Builder, Reviewer pipeline

```
Scout --> Planner --> Builder --> Reviewer
                         ^
                         |  (has_errors: fix)
                         |
                    Reviewer
                         |
                         v (needs_replan)
                      Planner
```

**How it runs:**
1. **Scout** explores the task, outputs findings
2. **Planner** reads Scout's output, creates a structured plan
3. **Builder** reads the plan, executes the work
4. **Reviewer** reads the plan + Builder's output, checks for errors
   - If errors found: routes back to **Builder** with specific fixes
   - If fundamental issue: routes back to **Planner** for a new plan
   - If approved: pipeline completes

## Proposed Architecture

### 1. Pipeline Schema (JSON)
```json
{
  "id": "dev-pipeline",
  "name": "Dev Workflow",
  "nodes": [
    { "id": "scout", "agentId": "researcher", "systemPrompt": "Explore the task..." },
    { "id": "planner", "agentId": "architect", "systemPrompt": "Create a plan..." },
    { "id": "builder", "agentId": "coder", "systemPrompt": "Build based on the plan..." },
    { "id": "reviewer", "agentId": "critic", "systemPrompt": "Review the output..." }
  ],
  "edges": [
    { "from": "scout", "to": "planner" },
    { "from": "planner", "to": "builder" },
    { "from": "builder", "to": "reviewer" },
    { "from": "reviewer", "to": "builder", "condition": "has_errors" },
    { "from": "reviewer", "to": "planner", "condition": "needs_replan" }
  ],
  "maxIterations": 5
}
```

### 2. Pipeline Builder UI
- Drag-and-drop node editor (React Flow)
- Connect agents with edges, set conditions visually
- Save/load pipeline templates

### 3. Pipeline Runtime
- Server-side execution engine (tRPC)
- Evaluates edge conditions from agent output
- Passes accumulated context forward
- Respects `maxIterations` to prevent infinite loops

### 4. Pipeline Run View
- Real-time visualization of which node is active
- See each agent's output inline
- Pause/resume/abort support

## Implementation Phases

**Phase 1: Linear Pipelines (simpler, faster)**
- Fixed sequence: A, B, C, D
- No conditions yet, just context chaining
- Prove the concept with minimal code

**Phase 2: Conditional Routing**
- Add condition evaluation on edges
- Support `on_success` / `on_error` / custom conditions
- Feedback loops with iteration limits

**Phase 3: Pipeline Marketplace**
- Share/import pipeline templates
- Community-built workflows (same model as Agent Marketplace)

## Alignment with LobeHub's Vision

This directly extends the *"Agents as the unit of work"* philosophy from the README. Instead of isolated agent interactions, pipelines make agents true **collaborators**, each playing a specialized role in a larger autonomous workflow.

## Willing to Contribute

I'm willing to work on this. Happy to start with Phase 1 (linear pipelines) as a PR to validate the approach before tackling conditional routing.

Would love to hear maintainer thoughts on:
1. Whether this fits the current roadmap
2. Preferred approach for the runtime (tRPC vs separate worker)
3. Any existing internal work on this direction
